nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
ن: on this word there are some thirty-odd answers: among them six meanings and six readings, one of which has six answers. Al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr reported from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said:
The earths are upon Nūn, Nūn is upon the water, the water is upon the rock, and the rock has four corners, on each corner of which an angel stands in the water. Yazīd reported from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «الر», «حم» and «ن» are the letters of «الرحمن» separated. In the ḥadīth of Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father, traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ), he said: Nūn is a tablet of light. Qatāda said: Nūn is the inkwell. Abū Jaʿfar said: these are four views. It has also been said: the implied form is «ورب ن»; and it has been said: it is a call to attention (tanbīh), as was mentioned earlier regarding «ألم». As for the readings, they are six, as we mentioned. Most people read ن وَالْقَلَمِ with the nūn pronounced distinctly; it has been read with it concealed (ikhfāʾ); it has been read with it assimilated, with nasalization (ghunna) and without nasalization; it is reported from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that he read «ن والقلم» [i.e. «نونَ», in the accusative] [Translator's note: the unvowelled text does not show the vowel]; and Ibn Isḥāq read «نون والقلم» in the genitive [i.e. «نونِ»]. These are six readings. On the accusative one among them there are six answers. Among them: that it is accusative by the action of a verb falling on it, i.e. «اذكر ن».
And it is not declined (lam tanṣarif) because it is the name of the sūra. A second answer: that it is not declined because it is a foreign noun. These two answers are from al-Akhfash Saʿīd. The view of Sībawayh is that it was likened to «أين» and «كيف»; the view of al-Farrāʾ is that it was likened to «ثمّ»; it has been said: it was likened to the nūn of the plural. Abū Ḥātim said: the wāw of the oath was dropped from it, so it became accusative by an implied verb, just as you say «اللهَ لقد كان كذا» (by Allah, such-and-such happened). Abū Jaʿfar said:
These are eighteen answers. On its being made quiescent there are two views. The position of Sībawayh is that the letters of the alphabet were made quiescent only because they are parts of the letters of nouns, so it was not permissible to inflect them, just as the middle of a noun is not inflected. Some of the Kufans rejected this view, saying: when you say «زاي», you have added an alif and a yāʾ to the letter. He said: sounder than this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who said: the letters of the alphabet were not inflected because you intended only to teach spelling. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound view, because when you intend to teach spelling it is not permissible to add inflection, for that would remove it from the sense of spelling — unless you qualify it with a naʿt (adjective) or conjoin to it, and then you inflect it. Whoever pronounces the nūn distinctly says: the rule for the letters of spelling is that one pauses on them; moreover, the nūn is far in its point of articulation from the wāw, so it resembled the guttural letters. For this reason no one read with the nūn pronounced distinctly in «كهيعص», because of the closeness of the ṣād to the nūn; al-Kisāʾī assimilated it because he built the speech on continuous reading (waṣl). Whoever assimilates with nasalization wanted not to remove the trace of the nūn; whoever drops the nasalization says: the assimilated letter has taken on the ruling of what it is assimilated into. Whoever reads «نون والقلم» gave it kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū Ḥātim said: he implied the wāw of the oath. If you put «نون» in the plural, you say:
«نونات», taking it as a letter of spelling; if you put it in the plural as a name for the fish, you say for the plural of multitude:
«نينان», and for the plural of paucity «أنوان»; «نونَ» is also permissible, like «كوز» and «كوزة». وَالْقَلَمِ: genitive by the wāw of the oath. It is the pen that one writes with, except that authoritative instruction (tawqīf) has come that it is the pen with which everything that will be until the Day of Resurrection was written on the Preserved Tablet. Al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazza reported that from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās; and Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra from his father, tracing it back to the Prophet. وَما يَسْطُرُونَ: a wāw of conjunction, not a wāw of oath; «ما» and the verb form a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which). The answer to the oath is ما أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ: that is, you are not, by what Allah has favoured you with of intellect and understanding — since he was the most intelligent of the people of his time — بِمَجْنُونٍ, which means one whose intellect is covered. From this comes «جنّ عليه الليلُ» and «أجنّه» (the night covered him); and from it is said «جنين» (foetus), «جَنَن» for the grave and «مِجَنّ» for the shield. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said: [al-Ṭawīl] 496-
وكان مجنّي دون من كنت أتّقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I was wary of was three figures: two full-breasted girls and one just come of age.)
And it has been said: "jinn", because they are hidden from people's eyes. Heard from the Arabs, against analogy:
«أجنّ فهو مجنون»; the analogical form is «مُجَنّ». Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he held to analogy in this, as though «مجنون» were said from «جُنّ».

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْراً: that is, for delivering the message. غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ: it has been said: it is not held over you as a favour; and it has been said:
not cut off.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: [you are] upon a religion. Abū Jaʿfar said: so this would be like his saying ﷺ: "The most perfect of the believers in faith is the best of them in character (khuluq)", i.e. the best of them in religion, way, school and obedience. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, was asked what the great character was that he had; she said: the Qur'an. It has also been said: it is the cheerfulness he had, his striving to meet people's needs, his honouring them and his gentleness with them.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ: that is, on the Day of Resurrection. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: I asked Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī about this, and he said: this is the end [of the sentence]. Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is "you will see and they will see in which of you is the trial (al-fitna)".
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the implied form is "in which of you is the trial of the one tried". Al-Farrāʾ said: the bāʾ is in the sense of «في» (in).
Abū Jaʿfar said: these are the views of the grammarians gathered together. We now mention the views of the exegetes. Sufyān reported from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid: بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ: he said: which of you is the mad one. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: in which of you is the madness. The view of Qatāda: which of you is closer to Satan. These are three views of the exegetes. On the view of Mujāhid, the bāʾ is in the sense of «في», as one says "so-and-so is bi-Makka" and «في مكة» (in Mecca); and the meaning on that is: you will know and they will know in which of the two parties is the mad one who does not follow the truth — in your party or in theirs. On the view of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk: you will know and they will know in which of you is the trial.
And «المفتون» in the sense of «الفتنة» and «الفتون» [i.e. a maṣdar on the pattern mafʿūl], just as one says "he has no intelligence (maʿqūl) and no firm judgement (maʿqūd raʾy)". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is among the best things said about it. The view of Qatāda is that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: That is, He knows best who has strayed from His way among the disbelievers of Quraysh. وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ: [those guided] by you and those who follow you.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: Conjoined (maʿṭūf), and not an answer; had it been an answer, the nūn would have been dropped from it. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ: he said: He says: if you would make concessions to them, they would make concessions. The meaning on this is: they wish you would be soft with them and not condemn their disbelief and sins, so that they would be soft with you, act hypocritically towards you and become bold in sins; and softness in a matter like this is the ruin of religion. It is taken from «دُهن» (oil); softening was likened to it.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: That is, everyone known for swearing falsely; when he is like that, he is contemptible before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and before the believers. Mujāhid said: مَهِينٍ means weak. Abū Jaʿfar said: on this view «مهين» is of the pattern faʿīl in its regular sense; and it may be in the sense of «مُهان» (despised).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: هَمَّازٍ: from «همزه», when he found fault with him; the root sense of «الهمز» is «الغمز» (pressing, poking). مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ: «مشّاء» is lengthened (mamdūd), because it is an alif followed by a hamza; the alif is faint, and the hamza, because of its remote point of articulation, is hidden, so it was strengthened by the prolongation (madda). Likewise the wāw when what precedes it has ḍamma, as in «السُّوأى», and likewise the yāʾ when what precedes it has kasra, as in «سيء بهم». This is in the connected case (within one word). [As for the separated case,] the grammarians have three views about it. Some of them said: there is no prolongation in it when it is separated. Some said: it is prolonged in the same way as the connected; Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] used to hold this. Some said: prolongation in the separated is more fitting than in the connected, so as to show by the prolongation the separation of one word from the other, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ [al-Baqara: 4], and likewise فَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَ الْبَشِيرُ [Yūsuf: 96], and with the wāw and the yāʾ: قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ [al-Taḥrīm: 6] and وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ [al-Dhāriyāt: 21]. Reciters are among the people most in need of knowing this. Mistakes sometimes occur in it, and that is a solecism (laḥn). Whoever reads دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ [al-Tawba: 98] may not prolong this, because what precedes the wāw has fatḥa; whoever reads «دائرة السّوء» [i.e. «السوء»] prolongs, because what precedes the wāw has ḍamma. This is required for the wāw only when what precedes it has ḍamma, and for the yāʾ when what precedes it has kasra, because they then resemble the alif and become letters of prolongation and softness (madd wa-līn) like the alif, so prolongation is required in them as it was in the alif. And since what precedes the wāw has ḍamma and what precedes the yāʾ has kasra, so that the vowel before each is of its own kind, they became weak and were strengthened by the prolongation. Whoever reads وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا [al-Baqara: 103] may not prolong this, because what precedes the wāw has fatḥa. It is said that most of those who err in this are reciters who recite according to the reading of Ḥamza. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever says «نميم» says «قد نمّ» [Translator's note: so in the text], «ثلاثة أنمّة»; and whoever says «نميمة» says «نمائم».

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: مَنَّاعٍ: a naʿt (adjective), and likewise مُعْتَدٍ; had they both been accusative, that would have been permissible as a naʿt of «كلّ» [Translator's note: i.e. of «كلّ» in the preceding verse وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ]; i.e. transgressing against people in his dealings. أَثِيمٍ: opposing his Lord in His command and prohibition, as Qatāda said: sinful towards his Lord.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
عُتُلٍّ: the exegetes, among them Abū Razīn and al-Shaʿbī, said: «العتلّ» is the harsh one. Al-Farrāʾ said:
that is, fierce in disputing falsely. Someone else said: he is the coarse one, severe in disbelief; its plural is «عتالّ». بَعْدَ ذلِكَ: it has been said: that is, in addition to that. زَنِيمٍ: also a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: أَنْ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "because he was". Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Ḥamza read «أأن كان ذا مال وبنين». Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said: this is by way of rebuke, i.e. "is it because he had wealth and sons that he disbelieves, or that you obey him?" [Translator's note: the text reads «أي الآن كان», "i.e. now that he had…"; this is translated according to the evident intended sense «ألأن كان».]

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views about it. Among them is what Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, who said: on his nose. Among what is mentioned is that Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ (16): he said: a disgrace that will not leave him. This is among the best things said about it, i.e. We will expose his affair and make it notorious until it becomes evident, and he will be like one branded on his nose. That said, it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās on سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ: he said: he fought on the day of Badr, was struck a blow with a sword, and it became a brand on him.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: إِنَّا بَلَوْناهُمْ: that is, We charged them with the duty of gratitude for favours and of giving the poor their rights, which We made obligatory in their wealth. كَما بَلَوْنا أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ: Ibn ʿAbbās said: they were people of the Book. إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّها: that is, they would surely cut [its fruit]. «الجِذاذ» is cutting; from it [comes] «صرم فلانٌ فينا» (so-and-so cut off ties among us) and «سيفٌ صارم» (a sharp sword). مُصْبِحِينَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «أصبح» means "entered upon the morning".

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: And they do not say «إن شاء الله», and they were blamed for this, because when a person says "I shall certainly do such-and-such", he cannot be sure that he will not be cut off from it and so be a liar; so he must say «إن شاء الله».

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: It has been said: a fire was sent upon it and burned their crops. وَهُمْ نائِمُونَ: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: That is, like something cropped, cut off. «صريم» in the sense of «مصروم», like «قتيل» in the sense of «مقتول».

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: أَنِ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. «بأن» (that); it may also have no position, being explicative (tafsīr). إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ: «كنتم» is in the position of the jussive by the condition; it does without the apodosis (jawāb) because of what preceded, since it is a past verb.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: In the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: The answer concerning أَنْ is as given before. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is without «أن», because the meaning of يَتَخافَتُونَ is "they say secretly".

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: The soundest thing said about its meaning is "with set purpose", as Mujāhid said: they had laid that down among themselves, i.e. they did it with purpose, groundwork and conspiracy among themselves, thinking themselves able to do it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, we have lost the way, and this is not our garden — when they saw it burned.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: It has been said: then one who recognized it and knew that they had not lost the way said: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ (27): that is, we have been deprived of its fruits because of what we did.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: قالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ: that is, the most just of them. أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ: that is, "why do you not" (hallā).

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: قالُوا سُبْحانَ رَبِّنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ (29). قالُوا سُبْحانَ رَبِّنا: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ: that is, we put the thing in other than its place by withholding what was due from us; and likewise «ظلم» (wrongdoing) in the language is putting a thing in other than its place.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: In the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا: a vocative of a muḍāf; the point of it is that its meaning is "this is the time for woe to be present". إِنَّا كُنَّا طاغِينَ: that is, in our opposing the command of our Lord and going beyond it.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: Sībawayh reported that some of the Arabs drop «أن» with «عسى», likening it to «لعلّ». إِلى رَبِّنا راغِبُونَ: that is, [desirous] that He give us in exchange something better than it.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: كَذلِكَ الْعَذابُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and likewise وَلَعَذابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ. It is called «آخرة» because it is last (ākhira) after a first; and it has been said: because it comes later for people. لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ: «لو» is followed only by a verb, because it resembles the conditional particles.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: جَنَّاتِ: accusative by «إنّ», and the sign of the accusative is the kasra of the tāʾ; however, al-Akhfash used to say: it is indeclinable (mabnī), not inflected, in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a second object.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: "Mā" is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is a complete noun, and لَكُمْ is the khabar (predicate). كَيْفَ is in the position of the accusative by «تحكمون».

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ (37): that is, do you have a book that has come to you from Allah, in which you study?

nahhas-irab:38-39.t: إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ (38): that is, for yourselves, against Us. «إن» was given kasra because the lām comes after it. Likewise أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمانٌ عَلَيْنا بالِغَةٌ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ: that is, or do you have oaths that We swore to you, extending to the Day of Resurrection, that yours is what you judge? In the reading of al-Ḥasan, «بالغة» ] is in the accusative («بالغةً»). Al-Farrāʾ said: as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "truly". Someone else said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «علينا».

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: That is, partners who help them and bear witness for them.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ: this is the reading held by the body [of reciters] that constitutes the proof; what is reported other than it is subject to inconsistency, as are most readings that depart from the body [of reciters], even if they occur in sound chains of transmission, since they come by way of single reports (āḥād). Among these is what was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, who said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read «يوم تكشف عن ساق» ("the day it uncovers a shank"), meaning the Resurrection and the Hour, because of its severity. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a sound chain, yet what we have mentioned occurred in it: as was read before Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī and a group of Sufyān's companions, who said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read «يوم نكشف عن ساق» with the nūn ("the day We uncover"). Sufyān al-Thawrī reported from Salama [ibn] Kuhayl, from Abū Ṣādiq, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he read «يوم نكشف عن ساق» with the nūn. Sufyān al-Thawrī also reported from Salama, from Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he read «يوم يكشف عن ساق» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the shīn («يكشف»). What the exegetes hold is that the meaning is "the day severity is uncovered"; that is well known in the speech of the Arabs. The meaning may also be "the day people uncover their shanks because of the severity of what they are in"; that is used in the speech of the Arabs. «ساق» is feminine and takes the hāʾ in the diminutive.
وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ: it has been said: they are called to prostrate only to be rebuked by it, and it is said to them:
"You were called to the prostration that would benefit you in the world, and you refused; so come, prostrate now" — because it is not an abode of testing and prostration does not benefit there. The meaning on this is: they are unable to prostrate with a prostration from which they would benefit. And it has been said: rather, their backs dry up [stiffen] as a punishment, so they are unable to prostrate.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: خاشِعَةً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَبْصارُهُمْ: nominative by «خشوع» [i.e. as agent of «خاشعة»]; it is also permissible to put both in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ: also in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; it may also be cut off from the first. وَقَدْ كانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سالِمُونَ: that is, in the world.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
مَنْ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined; or, if you wish, it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). الْحَدِيثِ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ: there are two views on its meaning. One of them: We will give them enjoyment and amplitude in this world until they imagine that they have good, and are deluded by the blessing and joy they are in; then We seize them suddenly, as Abū Mūsā reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives the wrongdoer respite, until when He seizes him He does not let him escape." Then he recited:
وَكَذلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذا أَخَذَ الْقُرى وَهِيَ ظالِمَةٌ. And it has been said: We will draw them step by step from their graves to the Fire.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ: with the yāʾ quiescent; the original is ḍamma on it, because it is an imperfect verb, and the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness. إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ: that is, strong and severe.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: The reading of Nāfiʿ is with ḍamma on the first mīm and the second quiescent. Abū Jaʿfar said: he brought the first according to the original form, and chose this because when it meets a connecting alif (alif waṣl) it takes ḍamma and nothing else, so he treated the disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ) in the same way. It has also been said: he brought both forms together, as he read مِنْ بَعْدِ ما قَنَطُوا [al-Shūrā: 28] and read لا تَقْنَطُوا [al-Zumar: 53]. Few of his companions or others argue for him [on this]. [Translator's note: the verse referred to is not quoted in the entry; it is أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ; the words discussed are not named.]

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ (47): Abū Jaʿfar said: this verse is among the most difficult in the sūra. The upshot of its meaning, according to what has been said — and Allah knows best — is: or do they have the Preserved Tablet, in which all hidden things are, so that they write from it what they dispute with you about, and claim that, despite their disbelief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and their rejecting you after the proofs, they are better than you and are upon the truth?

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ: that is, be patient in delivering the message, bear their harm, and do not hasten the punishment for them. وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ: in what he did, leaving his people and being distressed at the delay of the punishment from them. إِذْ نادى وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ: he said:
grieved. Abū Jaʿfar said: «المكظوم» in the speech of the Arabs is one who is grieved and finds no one to whom he can unburden himself; he has suppressed (kaẓama) his anger, i.e. concealed it.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, «لولا أن تداركته», making «نعمة» feminine; and the masculine is used because it is a non-real feminine. It is reported from al-Aʿraj: «لولا أن تدّاركه» with doubled dāl, the origin being «تتداركه», the tāʾ assimilated into the dāl. لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: It has been said: the meaning is "and He, Mighty and Majestic, described him as one of the righteous"; Sībawayh reported «جعل» in the sense of «وصف» (described). And it has been said: فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: Allah the Exalted granted him success in obeying Him until he became righteous.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
The Kufans say: إِنْ is in the sense of «ما» (not), and the lām in the sense of «إلا» (except). The Basrans say:
it is the doubled «إنّ»; when it was lightened, the verb came after it and the lām of emphasis became necessary with it, to distinguish between negation and affirmation. One of the Kufan grammarians mentioned that this is [about] affliction by the evil eye; one of the scholars considered him ignorant and said: they used to say only "we strike with the eye what we admire and marvel at for its excellence"; this is not of that kind; rather they used to look at the Prophet ﷺ with a look of hatred and aversion.
So the meaning on this is that, because of the sharpness of their look at him, they almost remove him from his place. One says «أزلق الحجامُ الشعر» and «زلّفه» when he shaves it. And it has been read لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ from «أزلق» and «زلق», i.e. in both forms.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the pronoun refers back to the reminder (al-dhikr) mentioned before.
